commitResults.messageBody: Reformatted all occurrences of "Duke" to "Dingleberry"

commitResults.messageTitle: Updated Dingleberry.java to greet and exit
commitResults.messageBody: Added horizontal lines and greeting message to main java file
Changed Dingleberry into command-line app. Reads user input, echoes each line, exits when the user types "bye".
Added function to save up to 100 tasks. Input goes into a str[] and list iterates all list items
Used constants for max tasks and seperator
Allows 2 new commands, mark and unmark and formats such that the done state is visible.

ToDos: tasks without any date/time attached to them, e.g., visit new theme park
Deadlines: tasks that need to be done before a specific date/time, e.g., submit report by 11/10/2019 5pm
Events: tasks that start at a specific date/time and end at a specific date/time,
e.g., (a) team project meeting 2/10/2019 2-4pm (b) orientation week 4/10/2019 to 11/10/2019

commitResults.messageTitle: Chat supports todo, deadline, and event tasks
commitResults.messageBody: This change adds parsing for todo, deadline, and event commands, creating the appropriate task types and printing the expected task-added confirmation messages. It also fixes the task type formatting so the brackets are displayed without an extra space before the task status.
Exception handling for Incorrect chat response

commitResults.messageTitle: Add UI test runner and refactor Dingleberry
commitResults.messageBody: Add a PowerShell-based console UI test runner and test plan, plus documentation for the test skill. Files added: .github/skills/test-ui/SKILL.md, .github/skills/test-ui/scripts/run-ui-tests.ps1, and test/ui-test-plan.md. Refactor src/main/java/Dingleberry.java to improve input validation, normalize the input loop (reads until EOF or MAX_TASKS), add helper methods (ensureCapacity, requireValue, printAddedTask), and centralize error handling via DingleberryException with clearer user-facing messages. Changes make command behavior deterministic for automated UI tests (unsupported commands now produce explicit error messages).
Delete function added + updated the list to Java Collections ArrayList<Task> instead
Used enums to consolidate commands to simplify code

commitResults.messageTitle: Merge branch 'branch-Level-7' Add feature for Level-7

commitResults.messageBody:
Extract UI interaction logic into a dedicated Ui class

Extracted all input scanning and System.out.println calls into a new Ui class.

Dingleberry now delegates all I/O operations to this Ui instance while leaving command parsing and core logic untouched.

Encapsulate task operations within a dedicated TaskList class

* Introduce a TaskList class that encapsulates the task list and its core
operations.
* Update Storage.save(), Ui.showTaskList(),
and Dingleberry to interact with TaskList instead of the bare ArrayList<Task>,
preserving identical application behavior and interface signatures.

Extract Parser class to handle command input parsing

Command input parsing, including delimiter handling, date parsing, index extraction, and argument validation, resides directly inside the main control switch of Dingleberry.

Mixing low-level string parsing with high-level application flow bloats the main class and violates the Single Responsibility
Principle.

Let's extract all per-command input parsing and validation logic into a new Parser class that returns ready-to-use values and task objects.

Isolating parsing logic keeps the command execution loop concise and makes input syntax and validation rules easier to test independently.

Existing test results and application behavior remain unchanged.

This commit encapsulates the chatbot's state in a Dingleberry instance, moving startup and the main command loop into run() and centralizing task saving in saveTasks().

The static main method now just creates the app and starts it, preserving the current behavior while creating a cleaner object-oriented entry point.

Introduce Command pattern for task operations

The main run() loop uses a large switch statement to control execution
flow, directly coupling command dispatch with task mutations and side
effects.

Handling execution flow via switch statements violates the Open-Closed
Principle and makes adding new commands error-prone as the application
grows.

* introduce an abstract Command class with execute() and isExit() methods
* implement ListCommand, DeleteCommand, AddCommand, and ExitCommand
* consolidate Parser entry points into a single public parse() method
  that returns Command objects
* replace the switch statement in run() with polymorphic execution

Adopting the Command pattern decouples input parsing from command
execution, allowing new commands to be added with minimal changes to
existing classes.

Existing application behavior remains unchanged across all test cases.

This change moves the core Java classes under a dingleberry package hierarchy (command, model, parser, persistence, ui, exception) and updates imports to match the new structure.

The refactor organizes the project into clearer modules without changing the app's behavior, making the project compile as a proper packaged Java application.

Add JUnit coverage for the common Task contract across pending and completed states. Verifies: description preservation, done/undone transitions, status formatting, and persistence encoding for ToDos tasks.

* Introduce ParserTest (JUnit5) covering command parsing for Parser: verifies recognition of 'bye', 'list', 'todo', 'deadline', 'event', and 'delete' commands and that ExitCommand/ListCommand/AddCommand/DeleteCommand are returned as expected.

* Add negative tests asserting DingleberryException for blank input, unknown commands, incorrect parameters (list with params, todo without description, delete without/with non-numeric id), and invalid/missing dates for deadline/event parsing.
